candidates.computation_change_reason: How 'WET' is interpreted in this document affects whether whole-effluent-toxicity results are treated as enforceable numeric limits (A), whether WET monitoring obligations apply (B), and how missing or non-numeric WET evidence is classified (C).

Whether a waste-load allocation is treated as an enforceable numeric discharge limit versus a planning or allocation concept changes which limit applies to a reported measurement and whether a compliance comparison is performed.

Interpretation of what counts as a water-quality-based effluent limitation affects identification of enforceable numeric limits (A) and whether associated monitoring or special-condition requirements are triggered (B).

References to a Water Quality Management Plan can govern permit conditions and monitoring obligations; different readings of what 'WQMP' incorporates could change which monitoring requirements are deemed applicable.

candidates.exact_span: As used in this document, references to State water quality standards and/or rules, regulations and/or management plans may mean the State of New Mexico and/or Tribal or both.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The permissive 'may mean ... and/or Tribal or both' leaves ambiguous which jurisdiction's standards, rules, regulations, and management plans govern; different readings could change applicable numeric limits (A), which monitoring requirements apply (B), and how missing or conditional no-result evidence is resolved when the governing framework is unclear (C).
